title: Refactor tooling is harness-native; daemon refactor surfaces retire with no bridge
content: Refactor tooling end state is harness-native, zero daemon reach-back. Refactor bindings (facts/algebra/apply choke point) run inside bro-harness against its working set — container test: harness + working set + spawned language servers must run every refactor binding with the daemon absent. The daemon keeps only dispatch composition and integration. The shipped daemon-backed path retires with no bridge: DaemonRefactor/install_refactor, the RefactorCapability trait, refactor_plan/refactor_plan_get flat tools, and the bbox_refactor_*/bbox_slice_* MCP adapters all die at used-kind parity.
rationale: Containerized/remote harness workers hold their own filesystem truth; daemon-resident LSP pools and plan stores would compute claims about files they cannot see (design/bro-harness/remote-worker-boundary.md). The refactor-tools gap cluster (gap-374fba64, gap-5d17610b, gap-de62454a, gap-903f6949) empirically showed the v1 MCP surface composing badly from code-mode cells. Sharpens refactor-tools-v2.md §7 "in-harness only (decided)": the interim RefactorCapability daemon path that shipped is on the kill list too, not kept as a bridge. Spike artifact: design/bro-harness/refactor-v2-pressure-test.md.
